method: EPA register 'National Grid Reference' and application-form 'Site Centre Point (Irish Grid Reference - 6 digits)' read as EPSG:29903 (TM75 / Irish Grid) and transformed to WGS84 with pyproj 3.7.1, default operation 'Inverse of Irish Grid + TM75 to WGS 84 (2)' (stated accuracy 1 m); the alternative operation (3) moves each point by 2.1-2.2 m. Read as ITM (EPSG:2157) every value would lie far offshore west of Ireland, so Irish Grid is the only plausible reading. The same transform reproduces the ie-p1 Clonshaugh point (318420 / 240501 -> 53.4015963, -6.2203039) to the stated decimals. Cross-check distances are WGS84 geodesic distances (pyproj Geod, WGS84 ellipsoid) to points of the merged national planning register (IrishPlanningApplications feature service, outSR 4326), whose point derivation is undocumented.

edgeconnex_newcastle_road_lucan.axis_order_review: Read literally (E 231915, N 302644) the point would fall at 53.9722037, -7.5143932, in the north midlands (Cavan/Longford border area) 100.0 km from the swapped reading, which contradicts the stated location (Newcastle Road, Lucan, K78 P3K1), the planning authority (South Dublin County Council) and the inspector's site description. Read with the values swapped (E 302644, N 231915) it falls 30 m from the national planning register points for SD19A/0042 and SD21A/0042, both described as the site in the townland of Ballymakaily west of Newcastle Road (R120), Lucan. Only the swapped reading is used.
